title: Push the cooker back so its rear foot goes under the anti-tip bracket
instruction: Push the cooker back against the wall so the rear foot nearest the black bracket goes under its hood.
context: Done by: appliance installers and delivery crews (O*NET 49-9031). Freestanding ranges must be fitted with an anti-tip bracket (UL 858): a floor hood at the wall that a rear foot slides under as the range is pushed home. The hood is hidden under the range by then, so it is lined up first. A range pushed home beside the bracket looks installed but can tip. Unlike TK-NKQG6Y (guides align a sled) and TK-KP8NWH (deploy a foot first), the robot must find the line.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x away from the robot, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top. Wall: a fixed grey box of painted plasterboard, 1 cm thick, 40 cm long along y and 12 cm tall, its face toward the robot at x 48, centred at y 0. Cooker (loose, 1.2 kg, painted steel, friction 0.3): a white box 15 cm deep (x), 20 cm wide (y) and 21 cm tall (23.5 cm to its top), its underside 2.5 cm up, on four steel feet centred 1.5 cm in from each corner (6 cm in x and 8.5 cm in y from its centre); each foot is a round pad 2.4 cm across and 6 mm tall on a post 8 mm across. On its front face: a dark oven door 16 x 12 cm and a steel control strip 16 x 3 cm. It starts with its front face at x 21 (centre x 28.5). Anti-tip bracket (loose but heavy, 3 kg, black steel, friction 1.2 static and 1.0 sliding), 5.4 cm wide: a wall plate 3 mm thick and 11 cm tall standing against the wall (its back 1 mm off it), and in front of it a hood 3 cm deep (x 44.6 to 47.6): two side walls 1 cm wide and 1 cm tall whose inner faces are 1.7 cm either side of the bracket's centre line, and two hood plates 4 mm thick from 1.0 to 1.4 cm up that leave an 18 mm slot over the centre line. The tunnel under the hood is 3.4 cm wide and 1 cm tall, open toward the robot. Lot A (the screenshot): cooker centred at y -1, square; bracket centre line at y 12.5. Lot B: cooker at y -2.5, square; bracket at y -6.5. Lot C: cooker at y -0.5 turned 5 degrees anticlockwise seen from above; bracket at y 5.5. Lot D: cooker at y 0.5 turned 3 degrees anticlockwise; bracket at y -12.5. Nothing else is on the table. Trials are run on lots A, B, C and D and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Per trial, judged at the end after the robot has let go (no gripper or fingertip within 5 mm of the cooker) and with the cooker still. The foot that counts is the rear foot on the bracket's side: the left rear foot (robot's view) in lots A and C, the right rear foot in lots B and D. To check it, look under the hood from the side or measure from the bracket's side walls: the foot's pad must sit between them. 1.0: the cooker stands on all four feet (each pad within 2 mm of the table), square to the wall within 3 degrees, its back within 10 mm of the bracket's wall plate, and that foot's centre under the hood: within the hood's 3 cm depth and within 6 mm of the tunnel's centre line. 0.25: standing and square as above, at least 5 cm further back than it started, and that foot within 5 mm of the centre line, but not installed. 0 otherwise, including the cooker home with that foot beside the bracket (looks done, not secured), or stopped short against the bracket. 0 for the whole trial if at any point the cooker leans over 15 degrees, or the bracket moves over 5 mm or turns or tilts over 3 degrees. Trials on lots A to D are averaged.
reset_notes: Slide the cooker out to its lot's start (front face 21 cm out, square or turned as the lot says) and stand the bracket against the wall on its lot's line. Lot A: cooker y -1, bracket y 12.5. Lot B: cooker y -2.5, bracket y -6.5. Lot C: cooker y -0.5 turned 5 degrees anticlockwise, bracket y 5.5. Lot D: cooker y 0.5 turned 3 degrees anticlockwise, bracket y -12.5. Nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0 and --epochs 4.
fidelity: About 1:4 scale. The cooker is a rigid box sliding on steel pads (friction 0.3); a real range is walked or rolled. The door is painted on. The bracket is a loose 3 kg part so the lots can move it; a real one is screwed down, so any move over 5 mm fails. The score checks that the foot is captured under the hood, as an installer verifies, not by tipping the range. Four lots stop a fixed habit, not a memorised replay of all four.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A, B, C and D); demo: 1.0 in each lot
